> A custom motion controlled digital bot which is shaped like a spider (hence the name Webbie). It has been designed sit on your desk (can also be used as a locket) and showcase its personality on a display. It has been equipped with a microcontroller, buzzer, motion sensor, display and environmental sensor, all fitted in a compact spider pcb design. I have thought of making the PCB black with cool red silkcreen spider stickers. Alongside the PCB, I have also made a cool 3D casing for the PCB. It also has some led's fitted on its PCB body!

## Design

### 2026-10-11 – **Webbie: Your Spider companion**

**6.18h**

**Webbie: Your Spider companion**

*Day 1       Part-1*
*Initiating the Schematic design*

I worked for 1 hour in which I made some great progress with the schematic design. This is my first non-ultra easy PCB design(did only 1 before, for LEDs lol!)  and am having second thoughts on whether it will work or not.

I placed all the components in the schematic and finished 90% of the wiring. Though I made some mistakes (like writing GPI'0{zero}'3 instead of GPIO3)  (I'll add more components later)

[In Timelapse attached]

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 015607](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Pt7NN3WWhsGmQH4spWLPF0N0AWTY2jCV/f726c7556bba16989d4badef2f9a1c3f0a56c374808025e72b5a63f80015f1ed.png)

*Day 1       Part-2*

Next, I spent 2 hours trying to assign footprints. I found it quite confusing as it was my first time + I didn't know whether it was fine using the ESP32 C3 SMD footprint or I had to use the ESP 32 C6 DIP footprint (as in the Starbie Github guide).

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 031154](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Pt7NN3WWhsGmQH4spWLPF0N0AWTY2jCV/92c1127407b2e4adf44c6b272653d4f1b25619f858362fe896f25c3d8ca53a5c.png)

Assigned all footprints and opened and opened PCB section! Only problem was that I had used the wrong footprint for ESP-32 C3.

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 175905](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Pt7NN3WWhsGmQH4spWLPF0N0AWTY2jCV/410346e3123279ba2957d1485a882ddd0d2db0a80f701a36d6bbe9b4237525aa.png)

*Day 1       Part-3*

Spent some of the time still solving the footprint issue and then used the ESP32 C6 DIP footprint and got the issue resolved.Next, I started searching for the perfect shape for my PCB until I found the perfect Webbie design!

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 212352](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Pt7NN3WWhsGmQH4spWLPF0N0AWTY2jCV/a265f86b23ae93356878e8159160e7beea14564999e1a343e9e5dc2cc1cb961c.png)

Next, Placed the components on top.

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 214620](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Pt7NN3WWhsGmQH4spWLPF0N0AWTY2jCV/646fbaa658837dd063c2eb8283ef463f3c976af5a2a43e4061c647187f2fb705.png)

Ngl looks pretty cool!

*Day 1       Part-4*

Figured out that I needed to enclose the PCB's Outline 100% and connect all the parts. I finished connecting all the traces (F. Cu and B. Cu).

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 223230](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Pt7NN3WWhsGmQH4spWLPF0N0AWTY2jCV/a2affd476c60d7975bcecb023bfd66aba08263d721c71f86c1c8c9c09a966bb3.png).

Forgot to connect the outer leg, lol.

Got some DRC errors and got a bit worried and started researching.
